claims.claim: Falden writes that it is rarely noticeable when Kay is explaining something purely for the reader's benefit, because the exposition happens together with revelations about characters.
Toyryla argues the narrator of Tigana often reports what the world seems like to an average person living in that world rather than simply giving information about the world as it is.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana', BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017 (hosted at BrightWeavings)
claims.quote: reporting what the world seems like to an average person

claims.claim: Toyryla observes that general facts about the storyworld of Tigana are often presented as something that everyone knows or as circulating rumours.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings

claims.claim: Toyryla writes that narratorial focalization in Tigana often takes the form of matter-of-fact description with only minimal commentary.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: matter-of-fact description with only minimal commentary

claims.claim: Toyryla writes that the narrator of Tigana does not make strong moral judgments, denying readers a guiding voice that would tell them what is right or wrong.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: The narrator does not make strong moral judgments

claims.claim: Toyryla shows that the shift away from the innkeeper Ettocio's perspective to the narrator's enables a matter-of-fact description of his execution.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: enables the matter-of-fact description of his execution

claims.claim: Toyryla argues that the Ettocio passage forces readers to see what the main characters' actions cost, though the main characters probably never learn his name.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: The main characters probably never even learn Ettocio’s name

claims.claim: Toyryla writes that the phrase 'according to most reports later' suggests the narrator is restricting his omniscience and narrating only what people hear about the incident afterwards.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: restricting their omniscience and narrating only what people hear

claims.claim: Toyryla notes that the narrator gives an approximate number of the dead in the Senzio massacre rather than an exact one.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: The approximate number of the dead could also point

claims.claim: Toyryla observes that the first chapter of Tigana does not claim that Duke Sandre is dead but reports that word went forth that he had died.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: the narrator does not claim that Sandre is dead

claims.claim: Toyryla reports that about sixty per cent of the text of Tigana has either Devin or Dianora as the focal character.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: About sixty per cent of the text has either Devin

claims.claim: Toyryla counts at least nineteen focal characters in Tigana besides Devin and Dianora, ranging from Alessan to an innkeeper named Ettocio.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: at least nineteen other focal characters that can be clearly

claims.feature: other: minor lives as world texture
claims.claim: Toyryla argues that focalizing a passage through the Governor of Stevanien strengthens the illusion of a world full of other stories around the one the novel is about.
claims.source: Roosa Toyryla, BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017, hosted at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: the illusion of there being a world full of other stories

claims.claim: Jo Walton writes that the world of A Song for Arbonne is portrayed beautifully, in effective, evocative and memorable detail.
claims.source: Jo Walton, 'Provencal Fantasy: Guy Gavriel Kay's A Song for Arbonne', Tor.com, 6 August 2010
claims.quote: The world is portrayed beautifully, in effective, evocative and memorable detail

claims.claim: Walton names it a problem of A Song for Arbonne that the world is more memorable and denser than the characters, who are gossamer by comparison.
claims.quote: the world is more memorable and somehow denser than the characters
